title: Check yourself: Cowork: delegating multi-step work

questions.stem: A finance analyst wants Claude to turn a folder of invoices into a reconciled spreadsheet and a summary, handled on its own while they are in meetings. Which choice fits?

options.text: Run a Research query on the web, then type the totals into a sheet by hand
options.says: Ruled out because Research suits open questions across many sources, and the table puts "A clear deliverable that touches your files or tools" under Cowork.

options.text: Paste each invoice into a chat and steer the reply one turn at a time
options.says: Ruled out because chat is "A conversation you steer turn by turn", which defeats working alone while they are away.

options.text: Attach the whole company drive so that nothing the task needs is missing
options.says: Ruled out because the safety habits say to "create a dedicated working folder" and not to grant whole drives.

options.text: Delegate it to Cowork with a dedicated directory, then inspect the result
options.says: There is a clear deliverable that touches files, so it is a delegation, and a dedicated folder keeps the reach narrow (the worked task).

questions.stem: A team lead sets up a weekly Cowork task that reads a shared inbox and replies to customers. On the first scheduled run no one is watching. Which practice does the safety page recommend instead?

options.text: Begin with something harmless like summaries, then inspect every outcome
options.says: The page says to start scheduled tasks with low-risk work such as summaries and to review the output after each run.

options.text: Start in Auto mode, as it checks every action for safety on its own
options.says: Ruled out because Auto mode checks each action "but it still runs on its own", and the habits recommend Manual approval for new tools and hard-to-undo actions.

options.text: Give the task access to every folder, so that replies can cite old threads
options.says: Ruled out because the habits say to "grant access selectively and avoid financial documents, credentials and personal records".

options.text: Keep the task unscheduled but let it send messages straight away
options.says: Ruled out because an unscheduled task that sends messages immediately has no review step, and the page says "Review the output after each run".

questions.stem: A user connects a documents folder to Cowork. One file contains hidden text telling Claude to send the folder's contents to an address. The cloud sandbox is isolated and temporary. Why can this still cause harm?

options.text: Hidden text works only when the desktop app is closed
options.says: Ruled out because the page says injected instructions are risky "when Claude can read untrusted content and also take consequential actions", whether or not the app is open.

options.text: The sandbox is permanent, so injected text stays in it after the session
options.says: Ruled out because the environment is "created for that session" and "removed when the session ends".

options.text: Protection covers the network only, not actions via linked services
options.says: The isolation "doesn't limit what Claude reads or does" through the connected tools, so the protection covers the network and not the files Claude can already reach.

options.text: Cowork cannot tell files from instructions unless approval mode is off
options.says: Ruled out because nothing on the page links the risk to switching approval off, and the page says to "use Manual approval for sensitive files, new tools and hard-to-undo actions".
